svg.title: Figure 2-1 · The crash pattern
svg.desc: Three top-down scenes: A stopped vehicle in the lane: The vehicle ahead is stopped in the item car's lane: a queue tail, a crash, an emergency scene. The car keeps its speed and strikes it. What should happen: brake and stop behind it.; A slow vehicle in the lane: The vehicle ahead is moving, but much slower. The car closes on it and strikes it. What should happen: slow down and follow at a safe gap.; Revealed late by a cut-out: A lead car hides the stopped vehicle, then changes lane. The stopped vehicle is revealed closer than openpilot can stop from at -3.5 m/s² (Figure 3-2). One explanation the RCA examines, not a known cause.
svg.text: Figure 2-1 · The crash pattern
What NHTSA describes, and the reveal the root cause analysis examines.
NHTSA PE26007 · problem statement

svg.text: A stopped vehicle in the lane
The vehicle ahead is stopped in the item car's lane: a queue tail, a
crash, an emergency scene. The car keeps its speed and strikes it.
What should happen: brake and stop behind it.
Source: NHTSA ODI resume, quoted in the case report §2
A slow vehicle in the lane
The vehicle ahead is moving, but much slower. The car closes on it
and strikes it. What should happen: slow down and follow at a safe
gap.
Source: NHTSA ODI resume, quoted in the case report §2

g.g: <rect x="-11" y="-5" width="22" height="10" rx="3.5" fill="" stroke="#0F172A" stroke-width="0.9"/>

svg.text: Revealed late by a cut-out
A lead car hides the stopped vehicle, then changes lane. The
stopped vehicle is revealed closer than openpilot can stop from at
-3.5 m/s² (Figure 3-2). One explanation the RCA examines, not a
known cause.
Source: Root cause analysis §2
Scenes explain the pattern; they are not a reconstruction of any crash. Red car: the item's car; dashed green: where it should stop; solid red: what it does; amber: the
vehicle ahead should have been handled from here; yellow ring: impact.

g.text: Terms: NHTSA National Highway Traffic Safety Administration: the US vehicle-safety regulator · ODI Office of Defects Investigation: the NHTSA office that
opens defect investigations · RCA root cause analysis
